In February 1968, the Federal Highway Administration reconsidered this request. Interstate financing was approved for the I-94 interchange on the basis that the freeway facility from I-94 to General Mitchell Field would be an exclusive connection between two interstate carriers.
Shortly thereafter alternative locations for the Airport

Spur connection were studied by the Wisconsin Division of Highways

and Milwaukee County Expressway Commission. The selection of alternative

locations for a freeway facility was controlled by air terminal facilities

of General Mitchell Field on the east and Interstate Route I-94 on

the west.

On March 25, 1969, the Division of Highways, in conformance with directives of the Federal Highway Administration, held a public location hearing on the proposed highway improvement. The public hearing was held to explain the exclusive 1.5 mile freeway-airport connection and the need for a freeway to carry the rapidly increasing volumes of vehicular traffic oriented to General Mitchell Field. The proposed corridor locations presented to the public are shown on figure 16. Section IX of this report contains a compendium of official testimony taken at the public hearing.
In August 1969, the Federal Highway Administration approved the route location, Corridor #5, as recommended in the Division of Highways Location Study Report and authorized them to proceed with design engineering.
